reason: China litchi-industry feature is an economy story (investment, overproduction, crashing profits) but a foreign-affairs section is a defensible home for a China feature.
A TV exporter's losses from declining sales and a customer scandal is a corporate-earnings story with no technology content.
Video-game publisher collapse and layoffs is corporate news but the games industry routinely files under Sci/Tech.
Tech-company quarterly earnings sit between Business and Sci/Tech.
A pension fund tendering shares in the Oracle/PeopleSoft takeover is finance news, but the software merger saga runs under Sci/Tech too.
Sprint/Nextel $35B telecom merger is a deal story that either section would defensibly carry.
A CNET founder's private investment fund is finance news with a tech-industry hook.
German economic growth forecast from research institutes is an economic-indicator story, not World politics.
A biotech trade council hiring the House Speaker amid a perjury probe mixes politics and industry news.
Senegal's president planning a military-style locust campaign is regional/government news, not science.
Phelps winning Olympic swimming gold is unambiguously Sports.
Daily stock-market wrap ('Stocks Higher on Strong Tech Earnings') is Business.
Nintendo raising DS console shipment targets is a product/console story with a corporate-forecast angle.
Post-hurricane price gouging is consumer/business news but also general domestic disaster coverage.
Scientists identifying which printer produced a document is a pure science/technology story.
Theatre reviews of Kevin Spacey's Old Vic debut have no science or tech content; entertainment falls to the World catch-all.
The visible text is an election/politics column with no business content.
Business publications honoring Apple's Jobs for innovation straddles tech-industry and business news.
Daily stock-market wrap with oil prices and the Google IPO is Business.
Canada moving to decriminalise marijuana possession is pure politics/legislation.
BAE Systems acquiring a US IT contractor is a corporate acquisition, not World news.
Malfunctioning biometric voting devices delaying the Chavez recall is politics with a genuine technology angle.
Analysis of Oracle's proposed acquisition of PeopleSoft is a software-industry merger story.
Phelps and the US relay winning Olympic gold is unambiguously Sports.
Trial testimony about PeopleSoft's CEO firing over the Oracle bid is a tech-company lawsuit story.
Death of the world's oldest man at 113 is human-interest general news, not Sports.
Oil futures hitting a record $53 is a commodity-market story despite the Nigeria/Yukos context.
Oracle extending its hostile bid for PeopleSoft is a software-industry merger story.
Gordon Brown rejecting the EU Commission's budget demand is politics-meets-economy.
A phone company paying a $400,000 do-not-call settlement is a regulatory/business story with no technology content.
IBM BlueGene becoming the world's fastest supercomputer is a pure technology story.
InfoSpace's share price and bottom line is tech-company financial performance.
A controversial video game (JFK Reloaded) release has nothing to do with Sports; games belong under Sci/Tech.
Business-software maker firing its president over sales and stock price is tech-company corporate news.
An opinion piece on preventing Beslan siege deaths is World news; the author's science faculty does not make it Sci/Tech.
Archaeologists unveiling a 2,500-year-old tomb and mummies is an archaeology/science discovery story, the gold label is right.
Daily stock-market wrap on oil and Fed comments is Business.
European bourses opening higher ahead of a Fed rate decision is a market story; the PeopleSoft mention does not make it tech.
Jets winning on a late field goal is unambiguously Sports.
Analyst commentary on Microsoft Media Center Extender pricing is a tech-product story with a market-analysis framing.
Paralympic closing ceremony cancelled after a fatal bus crash is both a sports-event story and a tragedy/general news item.
New TSA airport screening rules are government security policy, not Business.
LCD panel maker shelving a fab after a price slump is tech-manufacturing news with a corporate-finance angle.
A Lucian Freud portrait of Kate Moss going to auction is arts/entertainment news, which falls to World; Business is a stretch.
Boeing and Northrop partnering to bid on a NASA spaceship is space news with a corporate-partnership angle.
A teen arraigned for online threats and weapons possession is a crime story; the online element does not make it tech.
A Soyuz capsule returning ISS crew to Earth is a space story, consistently Sci/Tech.
Oracle winning the antitrust case over its PeopleSoft bid is a tech-company lawsuit/merger story.
San Francisco mayor urging an end to a hotel labor lockout is labor/business (or local political) news with no tech content.
Sri Lanka Telecom withdrawing a lawsuit over a damaged submarine cable is a corporate legal matter with a telecom-infrastructure hook.
